claims: improves risk-adjusted returns across various asset classes
equity-like returns with bond-like volatility and drawdown
over thirty consecutive years of positive performance
a-quantitative-approach-to-tactical-asse.finding: A moving-average timing model, tested in-sample on US equities and out-of-sample on more than twenty other markets, then in an allocation across five asset classes since 1972, gives equity-like returns with bond-like volatility and drawdown.
a-quantitative-approach-to-tactical-asse.title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation

claims: Since approximately 2009, short-term trends have ceased to deliver reliable returns.
Post-2008 trend PnL has collapsed on small-tick contracts across all signal horizons, while remaining essentially intact on large-tick ones.
is-trend-still-your-friend-a-microstruct.finding: Using about 100 futures contracts over 1995-2025, documents that short-term trends stopped delivering reliable returns after about 2009 and links the break to volatility-normalised tick size.
is-trend-still-your-friend-a-microstruct.title: Is Trend Still Your Friend?: A Microstructural Account of the Demise of Short-Term Trend-Following

claims: The overperformance of the proposed optimal portfolio, applied to cross-asset trading universe, is confirmed by empirical backtests.
optimal-trend-following-portfolios-2023.finding: Derives an optimal trend-following portfolio decomposed into Markowitz, risk parity, agnostic risk parity and trend following on risk parity components; cross-asset backtests are reported.
optimal-trend-following-portfolios-2023.title: Optimal trend-following portfolios

claims: We show, via a thorough theoretical analysis, that the optimal trading strategy is trend following.
Numerical simulations and backtesting, in support of our theoretical findings, are also reported.
optimal-trend-following-trading-rules-20.finding: In a bull-bear switching market with a hidden Markov regime, shows that the log-utility-optimal trading strategy is trend following; numerical simulations and backtesting are reported.
optimal-trend-following-trading-rules-20.title: Optimal Trend Following Trading Rules

claims: Removing the 125-day layer improves Sharpe ratios and drawdown efficiency while maintaining benchmark correlation.
The medium-term band contributes little incremental performance or diversification once short- and long-term components are included.
revisiting-the-structure-of-trend-premia.finding: Optimises the weights of trend horizons per asset; finds the medium-term (about 125-day) layer adds little once short and long horizons are included, giving a short-plus-long 'barbell'.
revisiting-the-structure-of-trend-premia.title: Revisiting the Structure of Trend Premia: When Diversification Hides Redundancy

claims: Significant advantage of trend-following rules in avoiding downside risks.
A higher positive trend direction ratio leads to poor performance relative to buy-and-hold returns.
trend-following-with-better-adaptation-t.finding: Out-of-sample test on four major stock indices of moving-average and momentum trend rules; examines how market conditions and the averaging window affect recent profitability and suggests a guideline for choosing the window.
trend-following-with-better-adaptation-t.title: Trend-following with better adaptation to large downside risks
